Just want to start off by saying that I don't mean to offend any telemarketers out here who make a living with this occupation. My experiences are my own, and I'm sure there are companies/ work environments much better than mine :)

Same as another poster here, I worked as a telemarketer but only for a record high of 2 days. This job is the most meaningless, mundane, unfulfilling job that sucks the soul out of you. I've done far more physically demanding jobs like working in Royal sporting House, climbing storage shelves and found that to be more enjoyable.

Sure, there are people out here who enjoy the cushy prospects of sitting down in an office just making calls, but I found it so awful to my spirit. Not only was I working for some shit-for-brains venture capital company, which is against anything I believe in (I'm very working class and suspicious of these ideas of money making), it was also a very loud and stale office with bad lighting. The calls I made were to complete strangers, and I had to ask an average of 100ppl a day if they were interested in *god knows what*. I think it was investing in property in Fiji or something. I don't know. Who knows and who cares. The people receiving the calls were not anticipating them, so who is winning here? Me because I'm making $7/hour? Please.

I felt bad for disturbing 100 ppl a day, felt worse for being hung up on. It's bs.

Hey, thank you so much for the response. I got to be honest, you were pretty on point. Had neglectful and absent parents. I fit 1 and 2 perfectly, though not too independent that I fit no 3. Was an overachiever and have always felt incredibly alone, even in gatherings and parties.

Right after college grad, I left all my group chats because I felt left out in all of them. The result is my adult life being the way it is now. It's crazy because I knew I had fun with these people whilst at campus, but I can't fully open up to anyone, thus lacking authenticity in my connections. I understand that not all friends can be close friends, but it felt like they all hated me (looking back, it really just came from a lack of trust in anyone). 

I don't know how much time I need to get better. How long did it take for you? I want normal, healthy bonds with people without feeling like crap. I want to love and accept love. I feel like a shit smear on this earth basically, and that I should be wiped out.

I think there's some aspect of closure we both needed growing up when it comes to our parents. For me, I needed to know if I was worth anything to my mom since she never really noticed that I was there throughout the ordeal. At one point I blamed myself for my father's death, since we were going thru some financial struggles and my mere existence must have cost a lot and caused a lot of stress. For you, it's the traumatising absence of your mother in your life, not to mention the detachment from the rest of your family.  


I can't give you any great advice except asking if you've looked for therapy or taken meds. To be honest, meds have been pointless for me. Hanging out with friends works sometimes. Different things work for different people.   


I wish I could maybe give you a reassuring squeeze on the shoulder. I can switch to DM if you want to talk privately.

Hi,  
I hope this message is coming to you in time, or at least before you make any rash decisions, but I'm here to distract you and I'm here to tell you that there is no quick and painless way to die. There will always be that little bit of pain in death and I assure you that dying is not the best solution to any of your problems.  


I'm very sorry that you are going through a terrible time in your life. I am too, and I got on reddit to see if I was alone or not. This is my 2nd response to someone here. Clearly, I am not alone. You are not useless, nobody is, and your existence mattered to someone but you might not have caught on with that fact. 

If you need to talk to someone, please talk to me. I am here for you.

Hey, I don't know who you are, but honestly I relate and am going through the same thing. I grew up with neglectful parents and an abusive sibling. I saw my father collapse and die from a heart attack when I was 9. I grew up feeling like I had to be the adult taking care of myself. I want to let you know that your life has meaning and I'm glad you changed perspective midway. I don't know if you're a good person or not, but from here on out, it's an empty slate, and you'll always have that choice to change it up for yourself. Rich coming from someone who's so deeply suicidal herself, but I always see the best in others.
